rationale: Evidence: iteration 10 (score 724.1) is the best raced design. Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) complete reliably, with oval finish near 2.0 s and s-bend near 2.2 s. Slalom is still almost always lost (1/20 finishes, progress 0.64, max_error about 0.061 against the 0.06 m limit). Mean rms_error on slalom is about 0.018, so the robot tracks on average and leaves the line at sudden alternating bends. Lowering base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1 at fixed sensor y=0.08 improved slalom progress (0.56 to 0.64) and slalom completion (0 to 1 of 20), so speed was a real lever. Sensor look-ahead has reached its limit at y=0.08, so the remaining lever is steering authority. Earlier, kp 3.7 hurt slalom and s-bend, but that test also changed the sensor layout and kd, so it did not isolate kp. Change (one variable): kp 3.0 to 3.2, a modest step. Geometry, base_speed 1.1, kd 0.8, ki 0.02 and last_direction line loss are unchanged, so this iteration measures the effect of steering gain against the iteration 10 baseline. Expected result: slalom max_error falls to about 0.058 to 0.060 on some seeds, slalom completions rise above 1/20, and oval and s-bend stay at 20/20. Hypotheses: (a) if slalom max_error stays at about 0.061 with no progress change, the limit is not steering gain and the next step is sensor layout or kd. (b) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 on any track, kp is too high for the damping and kd should rise to about 0.9. (c) If oval or s-bend completion drops below 20/20, revert to kp 3.0. Because this is the final iteration and the unseen track differs in shape, a small gain step is preferred over a large one to avoid losing the reliable oval and s-bend finishes. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness, to separate the kp effect on each track.
